title: Initial Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Method Registrations
summary: Registers the HTTP methods that were defined in RFCs before the IANA HTTP Method Registry was established, giving that registry its initial contents.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7237 adds previously defined HTTP methods to the IANA method registry. Its table also records whether each method is safe and idempotent.

questions: what is the http method registry
subtitle: The initial registrations of HTTP methods defined before the IANA registry.

tldr.problem: HTTP methods defined in RFCs before the IANA HTTP Method Registry was established were not yet listed in that registry.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7237 registers those previously defined methods and records whether each is safe and idempotent, with a reference to its definition.
tldr.outcome: The registry provides a central record of these method names and properties. RFC 7237 says security considerations for each method belong in its defining specification.

today: RFC 7237 is an Informational document that records initial HTTP method registrations. Its table refers readers to the specifications that define each method.

sections.title: The Purpose of the Registration
sections.content: RFC 7237 registers HTTP methods that were defined in RFCs other than RFC 7231 before the IANA HTTP Method Registry was established. It records existing methods; the specifications it cites define what those methods do.
sections.plainLanguage: Many HTTP methods existed before their registry. This document records those methods and points to their specifications.

sections.title: What the Registry Records
sections.content: For each registered method, the table gives its name, whether it is safe, whether it is idempotent, and a reference. The list includes methods such as ACL, COPY, LOCK, MKCALENDAR, PATCH, PROPFIND, SEARCH, and UPDATE. The table marks PROPFIND, REPORT, and SEARCH as safe; it marks LOCK and PATCH as not idempotent.
sections.plainLanguage: The table lists method names and two properties: whether a method is safe and whether it is idempotent. It also points to the document that defines each method.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 7237 says that registering the methods creates no security considerations by itself. Security considerations for individual HTTP methods should be covered by the specifications that define those methods.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry entries do not change how methods work. Their defining documents cover their security considerations.
